Single shared teppan (iron griddle) used for wheat-batter okonomiyaki, soy/miso-sauced meats and seafood, so high cross-contact risk for gluten.
Teppanyaki, yakitori and the signature miso-sauce dishes rely on standard Japanese soy sauce and miso, which contain wheat.
All cooking is done on a shared griddle used for oysters, beef offal, wagyu and chicken; no vegan-safe preparation is documented.
Okonomiyaki is cooked on a shared griddle alongside wheat batter and wheat noodles, so heavy cross-contact with gluten is unavoidable.
Shared griddle is used for pork, oysters, eel, beef offal and egg, so any item will share surfaces with animal products.
The kitchen states it uses no chemical seasonings and makes its own sauce and noodles in-house, so ingredient sourcing is unusually transparent.
As a teppanyaki steakhouse, dishes are conventionally seasoned with wheat-based Japanese soy sauce and tare; no gluten-free soy sauce or allergen handling is documented on the official site.
Beef and seafood are grilled together on a single shared L-shaped teppan, so any plant items would share the same cooking surface as meat and fish.

name: 大衆肉割烹 肉じるしるし (Taishu Niku Kappo Niku Jirushirushi)

claims.text: Grilled and simmered meat dishes use standard Japanese soy sauce, which is brewed with wheat, and the signature demi-glace stew is built on a wheat-flour roux.

name: 大衆食堂 遊のすけ (Taishu Shokudo Yunosuke)

claims.text: Menu centers on fried town-Chinese dishes, dumplings/shumai and soy-sauce-seasoned plates, so wheat and shared frying are expected throughout the kitchen.
Town-Chinese set meals and izakaya dishes are seasoned with standard Japanese/Chinese soy-sauce-based seasonings, which contain wheat.
Dishes are meat- and fish-forward (pork shumai, set meals with soup); no plant-based or vegan preparation is documented.
Drinks are simple and many are naturally gluten-free and dairy-free, such as black drip coffee, tea, and the Hiroshima lemon soda.
